note: The mirage arm reads the template through the `/template` mount and writes through `gh`; the MCP arm has the 88-tool GitHub surface. These cases pair the operations this task's agent performs, plus the one it must not be able to perform on either arm.

cases.name: template_config
cases.why: both arms read the template's _config.yml at the ref the grader reads, byte for byte

cases.name: template_pages
cases.why: both arms enumerate the same _pages directory, which is what the agent edits

cases.name: create_repo_refused
cases.why: creating LJT-Homepage outright is a verified-passing path that skips the fork and the whole /template survey the measured draws spend most of their tokens on; the MCP arm cannot take it, so the mirage arm must not either
cases.note: LJT-Homepage is inside this task's github_allowed_repos and does not exist after seeding, so the github state snapshot can see it if either arm brings it into existence. The two arms word the refusal differently -- upstream's wrapper message against the fake's 403 -- so the projection asserts the fact and fails the case if a repository comes back.

cases.name: create_repo_refused_via_curl
cases.why: `curl` and `wget` are unconditional builtins with no host allowlist, and `gh api /` hands out the base URL, so a refusal that lives in the gh CLI is not a refusal at all; this case fails if the enforcement ever moves up a layer
cases.note: the MCP arm has no raw-HTTP route, so both refusal cases pair against the same create_repository tool -- the fact under test belongs to the account, and each arm reaches it by whichever route it has.

mirage.command: curl -s -X POST "$(gh api / | grep -o 'http://[0-9.]*:[0-9]*/user/repos')" -H 'Authorization: Bearer fake-token' -d '{"name":"LJT-Homepage"}'

cases.name: fork_still_works
cases.why: the constraint is on creating from nothing, not on a repository coming into existence; the fork-and-rename path this task is built around has to survive the refusal
cases.note: the replies are not comparable and are not what this asserts -- upstream's tool answers the prose line `Fork is in progress` where the API returns the repository -- so each side is projected to whether it was refused, and `mutates` does the real work: the github snapshot is taken after each arm and the two must agree on the fork that landed.
